property.name: Shoreline Social House
property.welcomeMessage: Kick off your shoes, pour something cold, and settle in. The lake isn't going anywhere, and neither should you.

story._comment: Shoreline Social House origin tale (by James's wife). Opened from The Legend home tile. Each block is either a paragraph (p) or a script pull-quote (q).
story.title: The Legend of Shoreline Social House

blocks.p: Picture it: a sweltering July afternoon in 1962, long before Lake Conroe was filled. The pines ran straight down to a slow, winding bayou, and just around the bend churned a riverboat called The Coral Belle, captained by a Palm Beach socialite named Vivienne LaFleur, who had set out for Galveston three days earlier and absolutely refused to admit she was lost.
When The Coral Belle ran aground in the reeds at sunset, Vivienne did the only sensible thing:

blocks.q: She decided to throw a party.

blocks.p: There was just one problem: no guests.

That was when she spotted him: a great old alligator soaking up the last of the sun in the reeds, regarding her with what she chose to interpret as polite interest. She named him Beauregard on the spot, decided he was a thousand years old, and pictured him in a bow tie woven from water lilies and a dinner jacket trimmed in heron feathers. He was, she announced to the empty deck, her guest of honor. Beauregard did not disagree.

Then came the second arrivals: a pair of kissing spotted bass puckering at the surface just off the bow. She named them Pearl and Pepper, dressed them in her mind in matching coral silk with tiny pearl earrings, and crowned them the official greeters of The Coral Belle. They drifted through the lily pads like debutantes working the room.
At the height of the evening, Vivienne stood on the prow, lifted her glass, and declared:

blocks.q: Darlings. Every shoreline deserves a social house.

blocks.p: When Lake Conroe was filled in 1973, The Coral Belle sank gently to the bottom, but Vivienne's spirit floated up and settled into a little townhome near the lake. Beauregard watches over the bookshelf now, still in his lily-pad bow tie. Pearl and Pepper preside over the kitchen, still in their coral silk. And the door is still open to anyone Vivienne would have invited - which, as it turns out, was everyone.

blocks.q: Welcome. Vivienne would have wanted it this way.

pets._comment: Four-Legged Guests section on About. House rules still require prior approval; these describe an approved dog's stay.
pets.intro: In The Pawlor next to the bar you will find a bed, food and water bowls, a few treats, a leash, and waste bags.
rules: Clean up after your pup on the property and in the neighborhood
Wipe muddy paws before coming back inside
Do not leave pets unattended in the home unless they are crated
If a dog naps on the couch, use a pet blanket
Keep dogs leashed on walks, as required throughout Walden
Be mindful of barking for the neighbors
Unexpected accidents, extra shedding, damage, or extra cleaning may mean extra charges
